decisions.executionNote: Begin left-tube approach with elbow-up lift and gradual downward-facing gripper rotation; geometry estimated from live RGB.
Replan from interrupted pose using smaller rotation and translation increments toward left tube.
Align open left fingers over tube body and lower gradually to grasp height.
Use wrist view to center grasp lower on tube body and correct yaw, then close left gripper.
Lift left tube with closed gripper and inspect visual retention before rotating toward rack.
Tube retained visually; carry inward while rotating upright in small continuous increments.
Continue controlled upright rotation and approach left rack slot, keeping the tube closed in the gripper.
Finish upright alignment above the left rack opening; preserve grasp and inspect before insertion.
Lower upright tube toward left slot with a small lateral centering correction; stop above final depth for visual check.
Continue slow insertion toward required depth with slight centering; retain tube until seating can be checked.
Tube tip appears centered in the large opening; lower another 3 cm slowly to seat the low grasp.
Contact limits further descent. Open to let the tube settle into its opening, then lift clear and inspect seating.
Withdraw open left gripper to expose the released tube and assess whether it seated upright.
Return left arm away from rack while beginning elbow-up approach to the nearer right tube; keep arms in separate workspaces.
Advance right gripper over nearer tube with continuous elbow-up rotation; left arm retreats. Released left tube appears tilted and will need correction.
Finish right downward approach above tube, adjusting yaw to its diagonal axis; settle left arm near origin.
Lower open right gripper to body grasp height and refine tube-axis alignment using wrist view.
Close right fingers around the centered tube body, then make a small retention-check lift.
Right tube is visibly retained. Lift clear, then start rotating it upright toward the right rack opening.
Carry the retained right tube inward and continue gradual upright rotation, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Bring right tube above right rack opening while rotating almost upright; maintain closed grasp.
Finish right-tube vertical alignment and begin slow descent above the rightmost large opening.
Lower the vertical right tube toward seating depth, monitoring wrist alignment before release.
Tube appears to contact the rim. Shift slightly inward and toward the front slot center, then test a small descent.
Release the centered right tube to settle in its opening, then lift open fingers away to inspect upright seating.
Right tube remains upright after release. Lift and move the right gripper toward the remaining tabletop tube, rotating gradually for pickup.
Advance right arm over remaining diagonal tube at clearance height with gradual downward orientation.
Finish downward-facing alignment over the third tube while remaining above grasp height.
Refine third-tube body alignment and descend to grasp height with open right fingers.
Correct visible third-tube yaw mismatch and move grasp slightly toward the upper body before closing.
Close on the third tube's centered body and gently lift to verify retention.
Third tube is retained in wrist view. Lift clear while starting controlled upright rotation.
Carry third tube above the rack at clearance height, continuing upright rotation toward the middle slot.
Move the third tube over the middle opening, keeping clearance above the seated right tube while finishing its upright rotation.
Complete vertical alignment and lower the third tube over the middle slot, with a small inward centering correction.
Lower the third tube vertically into the middle opening, retaining the grasp until seating is checked.
Finish slow insertion of the middle tube, open to let it settle, then begin lifting clear for inspection.
Middle and right tubes appear upright. Withdraw right arm and approach the tilted left tube with the left arm for correction.
Approach tilted left tube's upper body with open fingers while clearing the right arm away from the rack.
Center left fingers around the tilted tube's exposed upper body; keep the right arm clear and return it toward origin.
Lower and advance open left fingers around the leaning tube's exposed body, while completing right-arm return.
Close left gripper around the leaning tube's body and lift it free slightly to assess retained orientation.
Tube is retained. Lift fully clear and gently correct its forward lean while moving above the left opening.
Left tube slipped and now lies across the rack. Open and withdraw slightly while preparing a top-down recovery; preserve the other two tubes.
Pause open arms to let the displaced tube settle before estimating a new recovery grasp.
Move left wrist clear to reveal the settled tube and estimate a new tabletop grasp without disturbing the two seated tubes.
Reorient left gripper for the reversed tabletop tube and approach along the left side of the rack at clearance height.
Continue left-side recovery approach with small continuous orientation changes toward the reversed tube.
Advance above the displaced left tube at clearance height and rotate the gripper to match its reversed axis.
Replan from continuity interruption: lower the wrist with smaller forward and rotational increments to retain elbow-up reach margin.
Use small increments to bring the reversed tube into the open left grasp while lowering to table grasp height; monitor reach and continuity.
